title.en: The Wind and the Sea Obey

main_point.en: Jesus is worthy of our trust.

christ_connection.en: Jesus demonstrated sovereign power over nature by calming the storm. Through His miracles, teaching, and most clearly, His death and resurrection, Jesus proved Himself to be worthy of our faith and worship. He alone is able to save us.

content.en: 35 On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let us go across to the other side.” 36 And leaving the crowd, they took him with them in the boat, just as he was. And other boats were with him. 37 And a great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling. 38 But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they woke him and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”

39 And he awoke and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. 40 He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?” 41 And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

Leaders: You exemplify how to trust in God’s care and provision. Even when the enemy wants you to forget God’s faithfulness, cling to the truth that He is sovereign and good, showing students He is worthy of their trust too.

“The squalls that fall upon Lake Galilee are often sudden and severe. On the east shore the mountains rise quickly to a height two thousand feet above the lake’s surface. When the wind is channeled through ravines that descend through those heights, the danger to an overloaded little fishing boat becomes fearsome indeed. When this happened to the disciples, they must have exercised all their skill and bailed as fast as they could, but still the high waves and wind brought them to the brink of disaster.”⁸

“Certainly Mark understood the meaning to be faith in the saving power of God as revealed in the action of Jesus. Mark likely intended to indicate that faith is more than intellectual assent, that it is trust in a Person. This kind of faith Jesus’s original disciples should have had and all subsequent disciples should have.”⁹

“Faith does not end when we accept Christ. We also need faith to continue to grow in sanctification. How does a search for evidence help here? We search to find what kind of God we are serving. If my investigation leads me to a God who does not care, does not show compassion, does not take care of the birds and the lilies of the field, then perhaps this God is not trustworthy. However, in Scripture we find a God who cared so much that He sent Christ. We find a God who heals outcasts. We find a God who weeps over the unrepentant. We find a God who feeds the hungry with a few pieces of bread and fish. If this is the kind of God we serve, we can trust Him to calm the storms or go through them with us.”¹⁰

One major theme of Mark’s Gospel was that Jesus has full authority over the world because He is the Son of God. Mark displayed Jesus’s authority over nature, demons, and death, all impossible for humans to control. Mark included events that would help people believe in Jesus and in His authority as the Messiah. We must also remember that the event in today’s passage is one part of a larger narrative about Jesus’s authority. Mark aimed to prove that all of creation ultimately bows to the Lord, and we should as well. Many scholars believe that Mark wrote his Gospel by gathering stories from Peter about his time with Jesus. Peter was in the boat during the storm and could’ve accurately conveyed the fear the men felt. This storm was more than light rain or a little wind; it was a dangerous and monstrous event. These men, who had fished on the Sea of Galilee all their lives, were scared they would not survive. In their fear, they modeled how we can respond to our fears: running to the Lord of all creation, who is present and in control at all times.

The person of Jesus Christ has two natures—the divine and the human. Scripture teaches He is fully divine and fully human. His divinity is on display in passages that describe Him as being equal with God (John 1:1-18; Phil. 2:5-11; Col. 1:15-20; Heb. 1:1-3). The New Testament also points to the deity of Christ by showing how He possesses attributes that only God possesses, how He performs works that only God performs (Mark 2:5-12; John 10:28; 17:2), and how He Himself claims to be the Son of God (Matt. 26:63-64; John 8:58; 10:30; 17:5).

LORD, WE BELIEVE YOU ARE IN CONTROL. WHEN WE FACE DIFFICULTIES OR STORMS IN LIFE, HELP US TO BRING OUR FEARS TO YOU AND TO TRUST THAT YOU WILL PROVIDE IN A WAY THAT GLORIFIES YOU AND IS GOOD FOR YOUR PEOPLE.

question.en: Last week we talked about the kingdom of God being the most important thing in our lives and how to make it our priority. How did you prioritize the kingdom of God last week? When did you struggle with focusing more on our worldly kingdom?

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You'll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:

question.en: WHAT IS THE SCARIEST NATURAL DISASTER? WHY ARE STORMS SO SCARY TO US?
WHO ARE THE PEOPLE YOU TURN TO IN A STORM, EITHER IN A REAL STORM OR A STORM IN YOUR LIFE?
WHAT DO YOU DO WHEN LIFE FEELS OUT OF CONTROL? HOW DO OTHER PEOPLE AROUND YOU TEND TO RESPOND?

content.en: A major reason we fear storms is because we have no control over them. Storms in our lives work the same way. We know that many situations are bigger than us, and even with the best people around us, we just can’t control some parts of life. As we’ll see today, Jesus has control over every storm, and He never leaves us alone in our fear and uncertainty.

cultural_connection.en: We don’t enjoy difficult situations; usually, we do anything we can to avoid them. Regardless, bad things do happen. Sometimes, we want to blame God or ask why He wasn’t there when we needed Him. We naturally question why God allows pain. Satan may even attempt to use our pain as twisted evidence that God isn’t real or that He doesn’t care. Storms do come—but not because God is uncaring or absent. Storms come because we live in a broken world. Sin entered the world in Eden and touched every part of humanity. Even nature experiences the effects of sin. While this may be difficult for us to see in our moments of pain, God hates our pain more than we do. He sent Jesus to make right what sin destroyed. The Lord is present with us in our pain. He walks with us through difficult times. He has ultimate authority over the world! God doesn’t keep His children from experiencing struggles, but He sustains us as we depend on Him, and through Jesus, we have assurance of an eternity free from pain and sorrow.

question.en: What was the disciples’ main fear? What did they not remember?

answer.en: Storms on the Sea of Galilee come quickly and powerfully. The men were confused and upset that Jesus slept while they were in danger. How could He ignore their circumstances? The disciples questioned Jesus because they didn’t fully understand His identity and His authority: God’s Son, Lord of all creation. At the core of their fear was the idea that though Jesus knew, He didn’t care. Like them, we experience moments when, though we know Jesus, we ask, “Don’t you see? Don’t you care?” We forget He is for us and with us. But our lack of trust doesn’t change the truth that Jesus is sovereign over everything.

question.en: When have you struggled to feel God’s presence during a storm in your life?

answer.en: Though Jesus doesn’t walk with us like He did with the disciples, He is with us in every moment and in every storm. As believers, we have the Holy Spirit living within us to guide, comfort, and encourage us. Maybe you struggled to feel God’s presence with you in a hospital room or when you lost a loved one, when your parents divorced or when you battled loneliness. You may not see Him with your eyes, but the Lord never leaves you. He isn’t unaware of your storms. He promises to use them for His glory and for your good Rom. 8:28)—the good of knowing Jesus and being made more like Him.

question.en: Do you think that the storm was a surprise to Jesus? Why would He sleep if He knew a storm was coming?

answer.en: The storm wasn’t a surprise to Jesus. In fact, crossing the sea at that exact time was His idea. He knew what was to come. Jesus was fully man, which means He needed to eat, drink, and sleep just like anyone else. However, Jesus was not only man; He is also fully God. Since He is fully man and fully God, Jesus knew the boat would be battered by waves; He knew the disciples would fear for their lives. But Jesus rules over the wind and waves; they shift at His command. He never lost control and knew His disciples wouldn’t be harmed that day, even though it appeared that way to the men in His care. What does this mean for us? Because Jesus was fully man, He understands what we go through. He can empathize with us because He lowered Himself and took on human flesh. Jesus being fully God means that all things come under His authority. These truths should help us remember that Jesus is compassionate and trustworthy. He is sovereign over all things, and we can rest in His care.

question.en: Why is the way Jesus calmed the sea significant?

answer.en: Mark’s Gospel centers on the theme that Jesus has authority over creation. Many people posed as possible messiahs, but Jesus was the promised One—the Word who created the universe (John 1:1-3; Col. 1:16)! We get to be in relationship with the One who created the storms and the oceans; He wants us to know Him, to walk with Him, and to be like Him! If Jesus has control over nature, sickness, and death and commands creation with only a word, then we can trust Him with every part of our lives.

question.en: Why do we struggle to trust God when storms come? How can storms either help or hurt our understanding of God’s character?

answer.en: Sometimes, you may feel like your life is falling apart. You may wrestle with unimaginable pain, fear, or loss. And trusting the Lord may be difficult because you can’t see any way out. The storm in this passage was one of those moments for the disciples. They couldn’t imagine Jesus calming the waters. Even worse, they couldn’t understand why Jesus didn’t seem to care about their safety. Here’s the tough truth: Jesus can calm every storm, but often, He allows them to continue. He chooses to reveal more of Himself by letting us experience wind and waves. Storms often open our eyes to a greater understanding of God’s love and care, reminding us of how desperately we need Him near us at all times. fo)

question.en: Why do you think the disciples responded the way they did to Jesus calming the storm?

answer.en: The disciples begged for help but were terrified when they witnessed Jesus’s incredible power and authority. This moment would help them confidently know that Jesus truly is the Son of God. Consider this: The severity of the storm is what helped them so confidently trust in Jesus that they later risked their lives to carry the gospel to the world. They believed so deeply in who Jesus is because they saw with their own eyes. You may not have a moment quite like this storm, but if you reflect on all the Lord has done to sustain you, you might be astounded too. Ask Him to open your eyes. Seeing Jesus’s authority can help you follow Him in confidence because you trust He sees, He knows, and He cares.

question.en: How can you pause to reflect on God’s sovereign care in your life? How can you live in gratitude to Him this week?

answer.en: We live busy, distracted lives, so we can easily lose sight of all the Lord has done for us. When life is painful or uncertain, we have a difficult time remembering how God has been with us in the past. And isn’t that what the enemy wants—for us to forget God’s faithfulness so we’ll be bound by fear and doubt? Taking intentional time to remember how God has been with you in the past helps dispel the lie that He isn’t with you now. Set aside time this week to reflect on the past, on moments that felt impossible to face; remember how the Lord was with you then and how He cared for you through other people. Write down what you remember. As you reflect on those moments, thank the Lord for His presence! When you spend time reflecting on the Lord’s faithfulness in your life, you’ll trust Him to be faithful again. This doesn’t mean you won’t struggle or face difficulty, but the knowledge that God is walking with you will change everything about the storm’s purpose and outcome.

content.en: The picture in a restaurant’s menu almost always looks better than the actual meal that arrives at your table. You order something off the menu because the picture looks so good, but when it arrives, you think, “What is that?” Many people can feel like this when it comes to their faith. People often make the decision to put their faith in Jesus and think all their problems will go away, everyone will like them, and they’ll never go through anything difficult. They think that following Jesus will exempt them from the harsher realities of this life. While Jesus does promise life, and life to the fullest, He was also transparent about our fallen and broken world and our very real enemy (John 10:10). Jesus assured believers that they’d face trials and tribulation, but He also assured us that He has overcome the world and will be with us in it John 16:33). If we follow Jesus, and if He is our example, then we shouldn’t be surprised when we face difficulties. Jesus faced persecution and hate. Jesus told His disciples that since the world hated Him, it would also hate them—and us, His disciples today (John 15:18-20). When we follow Jesus, persecution, trials, and tribulation may be a part of our lives. But we don’t have to live in fear or discouragement. Instead, we can take heart knowing that Jesus promised never to leave nor forsake us. We already have victory in Jesus’s name, and every trial is an opportunity for God to receive glory because of His power and faithfulness to us.

question.en: Have you ever been surprised by a difficult situation or season? How did it affect your faith?
How can knowing believers will face persecution prepare you to trust God and endure?

prayer.en: Thank You, Jesus, for never leaving me. Give me the strength and endurance to trust and follow You no matter what I face in this life.

content.en: Have you ever gotten caught in a storm without an umbrella? You probably got absolutely drenched. People often refer to the difficulties of life as storms, even saying the expression, “When it rains, it pours.” But what if we have an umbrella available to us when it rains and when it pours? In this psalm, David wrote from the experience of a shepherd. He knew the lengths shepherds go to in caring for their sheep: They stay close; they lead them to safety; and they provide for their needs. David explained that even when we walk through the darkest valleys, we don’t have to fear because God is with us (v. 4). God’s presence and His power not only keep us safe, but they also comfort us. Why? Because if God is for us, then who can be against us Rom. 8:31). Not only does God go with us and protect us, but He also provides what we need in every circumstance (v. 5). Therefore, no matter the storms we go through or what trials we face, we can have both confidence and comfort, knowing God sees, cares, and stays close. While this is true, something is required from us. Even if you have an umbrella in the middle of a rainstorm, it does you no good if you don’t open it and use it. Although God has promised to never leave us and to be our Protector and Provider, we must choose to come under His covering. How do we do this? We intentionally run to God, call on Him, and rest in His presence. We remain close to our Shepherd. No matter what rainstorm you find yourself in, remember that an umbrella is available to you—one that is more than capable to handle the weather and one that will always keep you safe. His name is Jesus.

question.en: How have you experienced God’s comfort and care for you during a difficult time?
What else are you tempted to run to during life’s storms? How can you go to God instead?

prayer.en: GOD, I KNOW YOU PROMISED TO NEVER LEAVE ME. HELP ME RUN TO YOU SO THAT I MAY EXPERIENCE YOUR PRESENCE AND POWER IN THE MIDST OF LIFE’S DIFFICULTIES.

content.en: When we’re afraid, we don’t act like our normal selves. Fear has a way of weakening us from the inside out. We can feel vulnerable and exposed. Our perspective becomes distorted, our attitudes shift, and our ability to make wise decisions is compromised. How we react to fear matters because we’ll face many situations that make us afraid. And in those moments, a wrong perspective or attitude can lead us to make really unwise choices. So what do we do when fear shows up? The apostle Paul explained that God didn’t give us a spirit of fear; He gives us a spirit of power, love, and good judgment. This verse is more than encouragement; it is truth that we can apply to our lives! The Spirit of God who lives within us as believers gives us the ability, even in the presence of fear, not to be ruled by it. Fear may lurk nearby, but it doesn’t have control. Instead, the Spirit empowers us to stand in God’s strength, to respond in love, and to make wise, steady decisions that are grounded in the truth of who God is and in what He says in His Word. And though fear sometimes feels very loud, God’s voice is louder. The Holy Spirit continually reminds us that God is with us and that He is our good heavenly Father (Gal. 4:6). As our good heavenly Father, God has promised to never leave us. He has promised to care for us, to guide us, and to be present with us in every moment. Knowing all of this should give us great confidence and help us to stand firm when fear tells us to run and hide. We can maintain a godly perspective, choose life-giving attitudes, and take faithful steps forward when fear would tell us to do the opposite. The next time fear creeps in, pause and remember that God is with you. Invite the Holy Spirit to strengthen you, to help you walk in love, and to guide you into wise and faithful choices.

question.en: How does fear affect you? When has fear made you act not like yourself?
How can you rely on God and call on the Holy Spirit the next time you’re afraid?

prayer.en: God, when I feel afraid, empower me with Your Spirit so that fear does not take control of my life.

content.en: Have you ever seen someone walk around with a “kick me” sign taped to his back without that person knowing? Because the sign is placed on his back, he can’t see it; so, he wonders what’s going on when people start laughing, or worse, kicking him! We don’t have eyes in the back of our heads, right? So, what’s the lesson? Well, in life, we can’t see or know everything. While we may understand this in theory, if we’re honest, we often live as though we can see and know everything. Living this way makes following Jesus more difficult because following Jesus requires faith 2 Cor. 5:7). Living by faith is often admitting we don’t know the way, we don’t understand, we can’t see what’s next. When we operate like we do see and know everything, we begin to trust only what we can see and what we can understand, a mindset in tension with a life of faith. God warns us against building a life that rests on our own understanding; instead, He urges us to build a life of full trust and confidence in Him. God promises that when we demonstrate this kind of trust by seeking His will in every area of our lives, He will lead and guide us, even when we can’t see or understand what lies in front of us—especially then! Shouldn’t this type of love and guidance give us great confidence? Yes! We get to rest; the pressure is off our shoulders to figure everything out because we have great confidence in our good God. When we rely on Him, He faithfully directs our steps and shows us the way.

question.en: Why can it be difficult to trust God when we can’t see where He is leading us?
How can you daily rely on God’s guidance rather than on what you can see and understand? Who can help you do this?

prayer.en: God, I make the choice today to trust in You fully. Lead and guide every part of my life and give me the strength and courage to follow as You do.

content.en: A soldier who goes to war is fully prepared for what lies ahead. They are prepared to face an enemy, prepared to face resistance, prepared to fight, and even prepared to die. They are not civilians; they are soldiers on a mission who’ve said “yes” to an assignment. In the same way, as Christians, we are not civilians but soldiers. The Bible clearly explains that we have an enemy and that we are engaged in a battle of faith (1 Tim. 6:12). Though we live in this world, we’re citizens of God’s kingdom; in a very real way, this world is not our home (Phil. 3:20). As believers, we live like soldiers—fighting the good fight of faith, representing God’s kingdom, and carrying an assignment or mission Matt. 28:19-20). Therefore, like soldiers who face an enemy, we too should be prepared for resistance, prepared to fight, and even prepared to die to ourselves. We often don’t think about life in this way; we don’t often view ourselves as soldiers from another kingdom. Then, when we face resistance or faith feels like a fight, we act surprised. Not only do we act surprised, but we also begin to wonder if we are doing something wrong! Peter wrote that we shouldn't be surprised when we face trials and tribulations, as if something strange were happening to us (v. 12). Trials are often evidence that we’re in the battle. Instead, we should consider it great joy because we’re on mission with Christ and are guaranteed victory in Him. So, like soldiers, let us prepare ourselves for what lies ahead. Yes—a fight. But also a victory! Jesus defeated sin, death, hell when He rose from the grave, and as we fight the good fight of faith, we can know His victory is our victory too!

question.en: As a Christian, do you ever feel surprised when you go through hard times? If so, why?
How can this passage give you strength and confidence during difficult times?

prayer.en: God, help me to remember that I am on mission with You, and that I am engaged in the good fight of faith. Remind me of the victory I already have in Jesus!
